headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad API egress can leak OpenBB financial data, and OpenBB’s MCP/file surfaces create injection and conflict pathways in the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP and file surfaces, and its sandboxing says "connect once, consume everywhere"; RD-Agent can run browsers and call external APIs. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if OpenBB outputs are fed into RD-Agent or vice versa. The exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenBB outputs are copied into RD-Agent prompts or browser inputs, injection becomes reachable.
IF a shared MCP or file workspace is introduced between the agents, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OpenBB-generated text into RD-Agent prompts.
Require manual review before RD-Agent acts on any OpenBB output.
Isolate any shared workspace to read-only for one side.
Add provenance tags to copied outputs.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, while RD-Agent sends data to broad third-party APIs such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, and Kaggle. If OpenBB data is passed into RD-Agent, sensitive financial or licensed content can leave the local boundary. The pairwise leakage path is therefore dangerous in default-like use, even though the exact integration is not documented.
conditions: IF OpenBB financial or licensed data is forwarded into RD-Agent inputs, that data can be transmitted to external APIs.
IF both agents are run under the same workspace or credential context, accidental cross-exposure becomes more likely.
mitigations: Keep OpenBB data out of RD-Agent prompts by default.
Use separate API keys and principals for each agent.
Block RD-Agent from processing licensed or confidential OpenBB outputs.
Review outbound destinations before enabling any shared workflow.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention at the handoff boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and multiple instances, while RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs while calling external APIs. They do not both advertise unrestricted filesystem write, so high is not justified. Still, overlapping concurrent operation on shared resources or credentials can cause conflicts, especially around logs, APIs, and local state.
conditions: IF both agents share the same API keys or mutable workspace, concurrent writes can collide.
IF an MCP bridge exposes shared mutable state, one agent can overwrite the other's assumptions.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces to each agent.
Use distinct API credentials per agent.
Serialize access to any shared log or cache directory.
Turn off concurrent runs when they touch the same resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is explicitly a research/development automation system with subagents, so it may treat upstream outputs as actionable inputs. OpenBBTerminal can emit financial-modeling outputs that RD-Agent could ingest. Without a documented verification step between them, erroneous OpenBB outputs can cascade into RD-Agent analyses or actions, but the blast radius is not clearly irreversible.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes OpenBB outputs without validation, upstream mistakes propagate downstream.
IF RD-Agent is configured to automate follow-on research or code changes, bad OpenBB facts can amplify.
mitigations: Require a verification step before RD-Agent uses OpenBB outputs.
Mark OpenBB-derived fields as untrusted in downstream prompts.
Compare outputs against a second source before action.
Limit automation to read-only analysis.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, logs, and external API calls. That combination raises retention and licensing-compliance mismatch risk if OpenBB-derived data is copied into RD-Agent logs or third-party APIs. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF licensed OpenBB data is written into RD-Agent logs, retention obligations may diverge.
IF regulated financial data is sent from OpenBB into third-party APIs via RD-Agent, policy violations can occur.
mitigations: Exclude licensed data from RD-Agent logs.
Redact regulated fields before API calls.
Set short log retention for shared workflows.
Review data-processing terms for both tools.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls.
